description: Social Justice question bank derived exhaustively from Indian Society and Its Dynamics - Chapter 5.5 (FDA & SDA Examination Notes). Every distinct point covered once; no duplicates.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.chapter: Meaning and Constitutional Foundation of Social Justice
questions.question: What is social justice?

options.A: Charity given voluntarily to the poor
options.B: The principle that every person should enjoy dignity, equal rights, fair opportunities and meaningful participation in society
options.C: A scheme for distributing free rations
options.D: A method of reserving all government posts for one group

questions.explanation: Social justice is the principle that every person should enjoy dignity, equal rights, fair opportunities and meaningful participation, and that institutions should address unjust disadvantage, discrimination and exclusion.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.chapter: Meaning and Constitutional Foundation of Social Justice
questions.question: What is the main objective of social justice in India?

options.A: To create a society based on justice, equality, liberty, fraternity, dignity and inclusion by protecting rights and improving the position of disadvantaged groups
options.B: To increase the income of government employees
options.C: To replace the Constitution with a new statute

questions.explanation: The main objective is to create a society based on justice, equality, liberty, fraternity, dignity and inclusion by protecting rights and improving the position of disadvantaged and historically marginalised groups.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.chapter: Meaning and Constitutional Foundation of Social Justice
questions.question: What is the difference between formal equality and substantive equality?

options.A: Formal equality treats people equally under the same rule, while substantive equality recognises unequal starting positions and may require special measures
options.B: Formal equality requires reservation, substantive equality forbids it
options.D: Substantive equality means treating everyone exactly alike in all cases

questions.explanation: Formal equality means treating people equally under the same rule; substantive equality recognises unequal social and economic starting positions and may require special measures for genuinely fair opportunities and outcomes.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.chapter: Meaning and Constitutional Foundation of Social Justice
questions.question: What is social exclusion?

options.A: The process through which individuals or groups are prevented from fully participating in social, economic, cultural or political life because of barriers

questions.explanation: Social exclusion is the process through which individuals or groups are prevented from fully participating in social, economic, cultural or political life because of barriers such as caste, gender, disability, poverty, religion or location.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.chapter: Meaning and Constitutional Foundation of Social Justice
questions.question: What is the difference between social justice and charity?

options.A: Charity is rights-based and structural; social justice is voluntary assistance
options.B: Charity is voluntary assistance to people in need, while social justice is a rights-based and structural approach to remove unjust barriers

questions.explanation: Charity generally involves voluntary assistance to people in need. Social justice is a rights-based and structural approach that seeks to remove unjust barriers, protect equal citizenship and ensure fair access to resources, opportunities and institutions.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.chapter: Meaning and Constitutional Foundation of Social Justice
questions.question: Which constitutional values are central to social justice in India according to the Preamble?

options.A: Justice - social, economic and political - along with liberty, equality and fraternity, assuring the dignity of the individual
options.B: Only economic growth and military strength

questions.explanation: The Preamble identifies justice - social, economic and political - along with liberty, equality and fraternity, and assures the dignity of the individual and the unity and integrity of the nation.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.chapter: Meaning and Constitutional Foundation of Social Justice
questions.question: Which Article directs the State to promote the welfare of the people by securing a social order based on justice?

options.A: Article 38

questions.explanation: Article 38 directs the State to promote the welfare of the people by securing and protecting a social order in which justice - social, economic and political - informs national institutions.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.chapter: Meaning and Constitutional Foundation of Social Justice
questions.question: Which Article directs the State to minimise inequalities in income, status, facilities and opportunities?

options.A: Article 38(2)

questions.explanation: Article 38(2) directs the State to minimise inequalities in income and to endeavour to eliminate inequalities in status, facilities and opportunities among individuals and groups in different areas or occupations.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.chapter: Meaning and Constitutional Foundation of Social Justice
questions.question: Which Article contains Directive Principles relating to adequate livelihood, distribution of resources and equal pay?

options.A: Article 39

questions.explanation: Article 39 contains Directive Principles relating to adequate means of livelihood, distribution of material resources to subserve the common good, prevention of concentration of wealth, equal pay for equal work, protection of workers' health and protection of children.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.chapter: Meaning and Constitutional Foundation of Social Justice
questions.question: Which Article directs the State to provide the right to work, education and public assistance within its economic capacity?

options.A: Article 41

questions.explanation: Article 41 directs the State to make effective provision for the right to work, education and public assistance in cases of unemployment, old age, sickness, disablement and other cases of undeserved want, within the limits of its economic capacity and development.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.chapter: Meaning and Constitutional Foundation of Social Justice
questions.question: Which Article directs the State to secure just and humane conditions of work and maternity relief?

options.A: Article 42

questions.explanation: Article 42 directs the State to make provision for just and humane conditions of work and for maternity relief.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.chapter: Meaning and Constitutional Foundation of Social Justice
questions.question: Which Article directs the State to promote a living wage and a decent standard of life for workers?

options.A: Article 43

questions.explanation: Article 43 directs the State to endeavour to secure, by suitable legislation or economic organisation, a living wage, conditions of work ensuring a decent standard of life and full enjoyment of leisure and social and cultural opportunities for workers.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.chapter: Meaning and Constitutional Foundation of Social Justice
questions.question: Which Article specifically protects the educational and economic interests of Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and other weaker sections?

options.A: Article 46

questions.explanation: Article 46 directs the State to promote with special care the educational and economic interests of weaker sections, particularly Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, and protect them from social injustice and all forms of exploitation.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.chapter: Meaning and Constitutional Foundation of Social Justice
questions.question: Which Article directs the State to improve public health and nutrition?

options.A: Article 47

questions.explanation: Article 47 makes improvement of nutrition, standard of living and public health among the primary duties of the State and also directs the State to endeavour to prohibit intoxicating drinks and drugs injurious to health except for medicinal purposes.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.chapter: Meaning and Constitutional Foundation of Social Justice
questions.question: Are the Directive Principles of State Policy enforceable by courts in the same way as Fundamental Rights?

options.A: Yes, they are fully enforceable
options.B: No, under Article 37 they are not enforceable by any court but are fundamental in governance
options.D: They are enforceable only during a national emergency

questions.explanation: No. Under Article 37, the Directive Principles are not enforceable by any court, but they are fundamental in the governance of the country and it is the duty of the State to apply them in making laws.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.chapter: Meaning and Constitutional Foundation of Social Justice
questions.question: Which Fundamental Rights are especially relevant to social justice?

options.A: Articles 14 to 17, Article 21, Articles 23 and 24, and Articles 29 and 30

questions.explanation: Important provisions include Articles 14 to 17 on equality and non-discrimination, Article 21 on life and personal liberty, Articles 23 and 24 on exploitation, and Articles 29 and 30 on cultural and educational rights of minorities.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.chapter: Meaning and Constitutional Foundation of Social Justice
questions.question: Who is widely regarded as the chief architect of the Indian Constitution and a central thinker on social justice?

options.A: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar

questions.explanation: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly and is a central figure in India's constitutional vision of equality, dignity, representation and social justice.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.chapter: Meaning and Constitutional Foundation of Social Justice
questions.question: What is a welfare state?

options.A: A State that accepts responsibility for promoting people's well-being through public services, social security, regulation, redistribution and protection against major risks
options.B: A State that provides only defence services
options.C: A State that does not intervene in the economy
options.D: A State that taxes only the poor

questions.explanation: A welfare state is a State that accepts responsibility for promoting people's well-being through public services, social security, regulation, redistribution and protection against major social and economic risks.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: Who are Scheduled Castes?

options.A: Communities specified for constitutional purposes in Presidential Orders issued under Article 341 in relation to particular States or Union Territories
options.B: All persons below the poverty line

questions.explanation: Scheduled Castes are communities specified for constitutional purposes in the Presidential Orders issued under Article 341. The category recognises communities that have historically faced severe caste-based exclusion and discrimination.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution deals with the specification of Scheduled Castes?

options.A: Article 341

questions.explanation: Article 341 empowers the President to specify the Scheduled Castes in relation to a State or Union Territory by public notification. Parliament may include or exclude communities from the notified list by law.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: Can the Scheduled Caste list be changed by an ordinary State Government order?

options.A: Yes, by a State Cabinet decision
options.B: No, changes can be made only by Parliament by law; a subsequent Presidential notification cannot independently vary the list
options.D: Yes, by a Supreme Court order

questions.explanation: No. Under Article 341, changes to the notified Scheduled Caste list can be made by Parliament by law; a subsequent Presidential notification cannot independently vary the list.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: Are Scheduled Caste lists identical in every State?

options.A: Yes, the list is uniform across India
options.B: No, Scheduled Caste recognition is State- or Union Territory-specific
options.D: No, only Union Territories have lists

questions.explanation: No. Scheduled Caste recognition is State- or Union Territory-specific. A community's inclusion in one State's list does not automatically establish its Scheduled Caste status in another State.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: Which Article abolishes untouchability?

options.A: Article 17

questions.explanation: Article 17 abolishes untouchability and forbids its practice in any form. Enforcement of a disability arising from untouchability is an offence punishable in accordance with law.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: Which Article permits special provisions for the advancement of Scheduled Castes?

options.A: Article 15(4)

questions.explanation: Article 15(4) enables the State to make special provisions for the advancement of socially and educationally backward classes and for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: Which Article enables reservation in public employment for backward classes that are inadequately represented?

options.A: Article 16(4)

questions.explanation: Article 16(4) enables the State to make provision for reservation of appointments or posts in favour of a backward class of citizens that, in the State's opinion, is not adequately represented in State services.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: Which Article provides for reservation in promotion for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes?

options.A: Article 16(4A)

questions.explanation: Article 16(4A) enables the State to make provision for reservation in promotion, with consequential seniority, for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes that are not adequately represented in State services, subject to constitutional requirements and applicable law.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: Which Article deals with the claims of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in services and posts?

options.A: Article 335

questions.explanation: Article 335 states that the claims of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes shall be taken into consideration, consistently with the maintenance of efficiency of administration, in making appointments to services and posts in connection with the affairs of the Union or a State.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: Which Article provides reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in the Lok Sabha?

options.A: Article 330

questions.explanation: Article 330 provides reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in the House of the People, or Lok Sabha.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: Which Article provides reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in State Legislative Assemblies?

options.A: Article 332

questions.explanation: Article 332 provides reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in the Legislative Assemblies of the States.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: Which Article establishes the National Commission for Scheduled Castes?

options.A: Article 338

questions.explanation: Article 338 establishes the National Commission for Scheduled Castes, a constitutional body that monitors safeguards and investigates matters relating to the rights and protection of Scheduled Castes.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What are the major functions of the National Commission for Scheduled Castes?

options.A: Investigating and monitoring constitutional and legal safeguards, inquiring into complaints, participating in development planning, evaluating progress, advising on safeguards and submitting reports to the President

questions.explanation: Its functions include investigating and monitoring constitutional and legal safeguards, inquiring into complaints, participating in development planning, evaluating progress, advising on safeguards and submitting reports to the President.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: Which Act protects civil rights by punishing the enforcement of disabilities arising from untouchability?

options.A: The Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955

questions.explanation: The Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955, provides for punishment for the enforcement of disabilities arising from untouchability.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: Which Act addresses atrocities and specified offences against Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes?

options.A: The Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989
options.B: The Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955

questions.explanation: The Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, provides for prevention of specified offences and atrocities, special courts, relief and rehabilitation measures and related safeguards.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What is the purpose of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Rules, 1995?

options.A: They prescribe procedures and responsibilities for implementing the 1989 Act, including preventive measures, investigation, relief and rehabilitation

questions.explanation: The Rules prescribe procedures and responsibilities for implementing the 1989 Act, including preventive measures, investigation, relief and rehabilitation, and the functioning of special courts and authorities.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What is the purpose of reservation for Scheduled Castes?

options.A: It is an affirmative-action measure to improve representation and access to education, public employment and elected institutions for historically excluded communities
options.B: It is a poverty alleviation scheme

questions.explanation: Reservation is an affirmative-action measure intended to improve representation and access to education, public employment and elected institutions for communities historically subjected to caste-based exclusion, in accordance with constitutional provisions and applicable laws.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: Which of the following are important Central Government welfare measures for Scheduled Caste students?

options.A: Pre-Matric and Post-Matric Scholarship schemes, Top Class Education, National Fellowship, National Overseas Scholarship and SHRESHTA

questions.explanation: Important measures include Pre-Matric and Post-Matric Scholarship schemes, Top Class Education for SC students, National Fellowship for SC students, National Overseas Scholarship and residential education support through schemes such as SHRESHTA, subject to current eligibility rules.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What is PM-AJAY?

options.A: Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana, aimed at reducing poverty among Scheduled Caste communities
options.B: A pension scheme for all citizens

questions.explanation: Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY) is a Central Government scheme aimed at reducing poverty among Scheduled Caste communities through livelihood opportunities, development of SC-dominated villages and infrastructure and related socio-economic projects.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What is the SHRESHTA scheme?

options.A: Scheme for Residential Education for Students in High Schools in Targeted Areas, supporting quality residential education for eligible Scheduled Caste students

questions.explanation: The Scheme for Residential Education for Students in High Schools in Targeted Areas (SHRESHTA) supports quality residential education for eligible Scheduled Caste students through identified schools and related arrangements.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What is the importance of education and representation for Scheduled Castes?

options.A: Education improves skills and access to opportunities, while representation supports participation in public institutions and decision-making; both are important for dignity, equality and effective use of constitutional safeguards
options.B: Only education matters; representation is irrelevant
options.C: Only representation matters; education is irrelevant

questions.explanation: Education improves skills and access to opportunities, while representation supports participation in public institutions and decision-making. Both are important for dignity, equality and the effective use of constitutional safeguards.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: Who are Scheduled Tribes?

options.A: Tribal communities specified for constitutional purposes in Presidential Orders under Article 342 for particular States or Union Territories, diverse in language, culture, livelihood, history and social organisation

questions.explanation: Scheduled Tribes are tribal communities specified for constitutional purposes in Presidential Orders under Article 342 for particular States or Union Territories. The communities are diverse in language, culture, livelihood, history and social organisation.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution deals with the specification of Scheduled Tribes?

options.A: Article 342

questions.explanation: Article 342 empowers the President to specify Scheduled Tribes in relation to a State or Union Territory by public notification. Parliament may include or exclude communities from the notified list by law.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: Are Scheduled Tribe lists the same throughout India?

options.A: Yes, one uniform list applies
options.B: No, Scheduled Tribe recognition is specific to the relevant State or Union Territory; a community may be a Scheduled Tribe in one State but not another
options.C: No, only Union Territories have tribal lists
options.D: Yes, only for the Sixth Schedule areas

questions.explanation: No. Scheduled Tribe recognition is specific to the relevant State or Union Territory. A community may be recognised as a Scheduled Tribe in one State or area but not necessarily in another.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: Which constitutional Article deals with the administration of Scheduled Areas and tribal areas?

options.A: Article 244

questions.explanation: Article 244 provides for the administration of Scheduled Areas and tribal areas in accordance with the Fifth and Sixth Schedules of the Constitution.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What is the Fifth Schedule?

options.A: It deals with the administration and control of Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes in States other than those covered by the Sixth Schedule, providing for Tribes Advisory Councils and special responsibilities of the Governor and Union
options.B: It deals with tribal areas in Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram

questions.explanation: The Fifth Schedule deals with the administration and control of Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes in States other than the tribal areas covered by the Sixth Schedule. It provides for mechanisms such as Tribes Advisory Councils and special responsibilities of the Governor and Union.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: Which four States have Sixth Schedule autonomous district council arrangements?

options.A: Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram
options.B: Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh

questions.explanation: The Sixth Schedule applies to specified tribal areas in Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram. It provides for Autonomous District Councils and, where applicable, Regional Councils.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What is the purpose of the Fifth and Sixth Schedules?

options.A: They provide special constitutional arrangements for administration, protection of tribal interests, customary institutions, land and resource-related concerns and local self-government in specified tribal areas

questions.explanation: They provide special constitutional arrangements for administration, protection of tribal interests, customary institutions, land and resource-related concerns, and local self-government in specified tribal areas.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What is the Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996?

options.A: It extends the Panchayati Raj framework to Fifth Schedule Areas with modifications to strengthen Gram Sabhas, protect customary practices and community resources and increase local participation
options.B: It extends reservation to private companies

questions.explanation: The PESA Act, 1996, extends the Panchayati Raj framework to Fifth Schedule Areas with modifications intended to strengthen Gram Sabhas, protect customary practices and community resources, and increase local participation.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What is the Forest Rights Act, 2006?

options.A: The Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006, recognises and vests specified individual and community forest rights in eligible forest-dwelling Scheduled Tribes and other traditional forest dwellers
options.C: An Act to ban shifting cultivation
options.D: An Act to establish the Ministry of Tribal Affairs

questions.explanation: The Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006, recognises and vests specified individual and community forest rights in eligible forest-dwelling Scheduled Tribes and other traditional forest dwellers, subject to statutory conditions.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: Which Article establishes the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes?

options.A: Article 338A

questions.explanation: Article 338A establishes the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes, a constitutional body that monitors safeguards, examines complaints and advises on matters relating to the welfare and development of Scheduled Tribes.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What is the role of Article 275(1) in tribal welfare?

options.A: It provides for grants-in-aid from the Union to certain States, including grants for raising the level of administration of Scheduled Areas and the welfare of Scheduled Tribes
options.D: It deals with the Fifth Schedule

questions.explanation: Article 275(1) provides for grants-in-aid from the Union to certain States, including grants for raising the level of administration of Scheduled Areas and the welfare of Scheduled Tribes, in accordance with constitutional provisions.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What are Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups?

options.A: A sub-category of Scheduled Tribes identified for focused support because of factors such as pre-agricultural technology, low literacy, economic vulnerability and stagnant or declining population
options.B: All Scheduled Tribes in the Sixth Schedule

questions.explanation: Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs) are a sub-category of Scheduled Tribes identified for focused support because of factors such as pre-agricultural levels of technology, low literacy, economic vulnerability and stagnant or declining population.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: How many PVTG communities are recognised by the Government of India, and across how many States and Union Territories?

options.A: 75 PVTGs across 18 States and one Union Territory

questions.explanation: The Government of India identifies 75 Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups across 18 States and one Union Territory.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What is PM-JANMAN?

options.A: Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan, launched in 2023-24 to improve basic services and socio-economic conditions in PVTG habitations
options.B: A scholarship scheme for SC students

questions.explanation: Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM-JANMAN) is a mission launched in 2023-24 to improve basic services and socio-economic conditions in PVTG habitations, including housing, drinking water, education, health, nutrition, roads, telecom connectivity, electrification and livelihoods.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What is Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan?

options.A: A Government of India initiative launched in 2024 to address gaps in social infrastructure, health, education, livelihoods and basic services in tribal-majority villages through coordinated action by multiple ministries
options.D: A scholarship scheme for OBC students

questions.explanation: Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan is a Government of India initiative launched in 2024 to address gaps in social infrastructure, health, education, livelihoods and basic services in tribal-majority villages and habitations through coordinated action by multiple ministries.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What do Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRS) provide?

options.A: Quality residential schooling for Scheduled Tribe children, particularly in remote and tribal areas, to improve access to education and educational outcomes
options.D: Schools for children of government employees

questions.explanation: Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRS) provide quality residential schooling for Scheduled Tribe children, particularly in remote and tribal areas, to improve access to education and educational outcomes.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What are common challenges faced by tribal communities?

options.A: Displacement, insecure land and forest rights, loss of livelihoods, poverty, malnutrition, limited healthcare and education access, language barriers, exploitation and cultural marginalisation

questions.explanation: Challenges may include displacement, insecure land and forest rights, loss of livelihoods, poverty, malnutrition, limited healthcare and education access, language barriers, exploitation and cultural marginalisation.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What is the difference between Scheduled Tribes and Scheduled Castes?

options.A: Scheduled Tribes are specified under Article 342 and Scheduled Castes under Article 341; both have distinct constitutional safeguards and separate constitutional commissions
options.B: They are specified under the same Article
options.C: Scheduled Castes are specified under Article 342

questions.explanation: Scheduled Tribes are communities specified under Article 342 and Scheduled Castes are communities specified under Article 341. Both have distinct constitutional safeguards and separate constitutional commissions.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: Why is community participation important in tribal development?

options.A: It helps ensure that development programmes respect local priorities, customary practices, livelihoods, language, culture, land and forest rights, and that affected communities share in decision-making
options.C: It is required only for Sixth Schedule areas

questions.explanation: Participation helps ensure that development programmes respect local priorities, customary practices, livelihoods, language, culture, land and forest rights, and that affected communities share in decision-making.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What are Other Backward Classes?

options.A: A commonly used administrative term for socially and educationally backward classes identified for specified constitutional and legal purposes
options.D: All persons below the poverty line

questions.explanation: Other Backward Classes (OBCs) is a commonly used administrative term for socially and educationally backward classes identified for specified constitutional and legal purposes. The Constitution uses the expression socially and educationally backward classes.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: Which Article enables the appointment of a Commission to investigate the conditions of backward classes?

options.A: Article 340

questions.explanation: Article 340 empowers the President to appoint a Commission to investigate the conditions of socially and educationally backward classes and the difficulties under which they labour, and to make recommendations.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: Who chaired the First Backward Classes Commission, appointed in 1953?

options.A: Kaka Kalelkar

questions.explanation: The First Backward Classes Commission, appointed in 1953, was chaired by Kaka Kalelkar. It submitted its report in 1955.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: Who chaired the Second Backward Classes Commission?

options.A: B. P. Mandal

questions.explanation: The Second Backward Classes Commission, commonly known as the Mandal Commission, was chaired by B. P. Mandal. It was appointed in 1979 and submitted its report in 1980.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What was the main recommendation of the Mandal Commission relating to reservation?

options.A: 27 per cent reservation in Central Government services for socially and educationally backward classes (OBCs)

questions.explanation: The Mandal Commission recommended 27 per cent reservation in Central Government services for socially and educationally backward classes, commonly referred to as OBCs.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: In which year did the Union Government announce implementation of the Mandal Commission's 27 per cent reservation recommendation?
questions.explanation: The Union Government issued the relevant Office Memorandum on 13 August 1990 to provide 27 per cent reservation in Central Government services for OBCs.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: Which Supreme Court case is associated with the 27 per cent OBC reservation and the creamy-layer principle?

options.A: Indra Sawhney v. Union of India (1992)
options.B: Janhit Abhiyan v. Union of India (2022)

questions.explanation: Indra Sawhney v. Union of India, decided in 1992, is the landmark case in which the Supreme Court upheld 27 per cent reservation for OBCs in Central Government services subject to exclusion of the creamy layer and laid down important principles on reservation.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What is the creamy layer among OBCs?

options.A: The relatively advanced sections of OBCs excluded from the benefit of reservation under applicable rules; Central OBC reservation is generally available only to eligible non-creamy-layer candidates in the Central List
options.B: A layer of SCs excluded from reservation

questions.explanation: The creamy layer refers to the relatively advanced sections of OBCs excluded from the benefit of reservation under the applicable rules. OBC reservation at the Central level is generally available to eligible non-creamy-layer candidates included in the Central List.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: Is the OBC creamy-layer test identical to the EWS income test?

options.A: Yes, both use the same criteria
options.B: No, the OBC creamy-layer rules and EWS eligibility rules are separate; OBC creamy-layer status includes status-based and income/wealth-related tests and should not be reduced to the EWS test
options.C: Yes, both use only the Rs. 8 lakh income limit
options.D: No, EWS has no income test

questions.explanation: No. The OBC creamy-layer rules and the EWS eligibility rules are separate. OBC creamy-layer status is determined under specific Government of India criteria, including status-based and income/wealth-related tests; it should not be reduced to the EWS test.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What is the difference between the Central OBC List and a State OBC List?

options.A: The Central OBC List determines eligibility for relevant Central Government benefits and institutions, while a State OBC List determines eligibility for benefits under that State's laws and policies; the two lists may differ

questions.explanation: The Central OBC List determines eligibility for relevant Central Government benefits and institutions, while a State OBC List determines eligibility for benefits under that State's laws and policies. The two lists may differ.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: Which Constitutional Amendment gave constitutional status to the National Commission for Backward Classes?

options.A: The 102nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 2018

questions.explanation: The Constitution (102nd Amendment) Act, 2018, gave constitutional status to the National Commission for Backward Classes by inserting Article 338B and related provisions.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: Which Article establishes the National Commission for Backward Classes?

options.A: Article 338B

questions.explanation: Article 338B establishes the National Commission for Backward Classes as a constitutional body.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: Which Constitutional Amendment clarified the power of States and Union Territories to identify socially and educationally backward classes for their own purposes?

options.A: The 105th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2021

questions.explanation: The Constitution (105th Amendment) Act, 2021, clarified that States and Union Territories may prepare and maintain their own lists of socially and educationally backward classes for their own purposes.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: Which Article concerns socially and educationally backward classes and the Central List?

options.A: Article 342A

questions.explanation: Article 342A deals with socially and educationally backward classes and the Central List, while allowing States and Union Territories to maintain their own lists for their own purposes under clause (3).

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What are the major functions of the National Commission for Backward Classes?

options.A: It investigates and monitors safeguards for socially and educationally backward classes, examines complaints, advises on socio-economic development, evaluates progress and reports to the President

questions.explanation: The NCBC investigates and monitors safeguards for socially and educationally backward classes, examines complaints, advises on socio-economic development, evaluates progress and reports to the President.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What is PM-YASASVI?

options.A: PM-Yung Achievers Scholarship Award Scheme for Vibrant India, an umbrella scholarship and hostel-support scheme for eligible students belonging to OBC, EBC and DNT communities
