questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What is the role of the National Backward Classes Finance and Development Corporation?

options.A: It supports the economic development of eligible backward-class beneficiaries through concessional finance, skill development and related livelihood assistance

questions.explanation: The National Backward Classes Finance and Development Corporation (NBCFDC) supports the economic development of eligible backward-class beneficiaries through concessional finance, skill development and related livelihood assistance.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What are major challenges faced by OBC communities?

options.A: Unequal access to quality education, employment and assets, social discrimination, regional disparities, under-representation in some sectors and difficulties in accessing welfare schemes

questions.explanation: Challenges may include unequal access to quality education, employment and assets, social discrimination, regional disparities, under-representation in some sectors and difficulties in accessing welfare schemes.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: Why must candidates check whether their caste is in the Central List or State List?

options.A: A caste's inclusion in one list does not automatically establish eligibility under the other list; candidates must use the list and certificate requirements specified in the relevant recruitment or admission notification
options.B: Because the Central List is always applicable to State recruitment
options.C: Because State Lists have no legal validity
options.D: Because all castes are in both lists

questions.explanation: A caste's inclusion in one list does not automatically establish eligibility under the other list. Candidates must use the list and certificate requirements specified in the relevant Central or State recruitment or admission notification.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What is a minority in the context of the National Commission for Minorities Act, 1992?

options.A: A community notified as such by the Central Government under Section 2(c) of the Act
options.B: Any group smaller than 50 per cent of the population

questions.explanation: For the purposes of the National Commission for Minorities Act, 1992, a minority is a community notified as such by the Central Government under Section 2(c).

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: Which six religious communities are notified as minorities by the Central Government?

options.A: Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists, Parsis and Jains
options.B: Muslims, Christians, Hindus, Sikhs, Buddhists and Jains
options.C: Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists, Parsis and Jews
options.D: Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists, Jains and Bahais

questions.explanation: The six centrally notified religious minority communities are Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists, Parsis and Jains.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: Which law provides for the National Commission for Minorities?

options.A: The National Commission for Minorities Act, 1992
options.D: The National Commission for Minorities Act, 2004

questions.explanation: The National Commission for Minorities Act, 1992, provides for the National Commission for Minorities as a statutory body.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: Is the National Commission for Minorities a constitutional body?

options.A: Yes, it is established under Article 338
options.B: No, it is a statutory body established under the National Commission for Minorities Act, 1992
options.D: No, it is a private body

questions.explanation: No. The National Commission for Minorities is a statutory body established under the National Commission for Minorities Act, 1992; it is not a constitutional body.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What are the major functions of the National Commission for Minorities?

options.A: It evaluates minority development, monitors constitutional and legal safeguards, examines complaints of deprivation of rights, recommends measures to governments, conducts studies and submits reports
options.B: It conducts elections for minority seats
options.D: It appoints judges to minority courts

questions.explanation: The Commission evaluates minority development, monitors constitutional and legal safeguards, examines complaints of deprivation of rights, recommends measures to governments, conducts studies and submits reports.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: Which constitutional Articles protect the cultural and educational rights of minorities?

options.A: Articles 29 and 30

questions.explanation: Articles 29 and 30 protect specified cultural and educational rights. These provisions also protect linguistic minorities.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What does Article 29(1) protect?

options.A: The right of any section of citizens residing in India, having a distinct language, script or culture, to conserve the same
options.B: The right to establish minority institutions
options.D: The right to equality in employment

questions.explanation: Article 29(1) gives any section of citizens residing in India or any part of it, having a distinct language, script or culture, the right to conserve the same.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What does Article 29(2) prohibit?

options.A: Denial of admission to any citizen into an educational institution maintained by the State or receiving State aid on grounds only of religion, race, caste or language

questions.explanation: Article 29(2) prohibits denial of admission to any citizen into an educational institution maintained by the State or receiving State aid on grounds only of religion, race, caste or language.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What does Article 30(1) provide?

options.A: All religious and linguistic minorities have the right to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice, subject to the constitutional framework
options.B: The right to conserve language and script
options.C: The right to reservation in employment
options.D: The right to free education up to age 14

questions.explanation: Article 30(1) gives all religious and linguistic minorities the right to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice, subject to the constitutional framework.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What is a linguistic minority?

options.A: A group whose language differs from that of the majority in the relevant State or area; the language need not be in the Eighth Schedule to qualify as a distinct language for this purpose
options.C: A group whose language is in the Eighth Schedule only

questions.explanation: A linguistic minority is a group whose language differs from that of the majority in the relevant State or area. A language need not be included in the Eighth Schedule to qualify as a distinct language for this purpose.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: Which Article provides for a Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities?

options.A: Article 350B

questions.explanation: Article 350B provides for a Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities, appointed by the President, to investigate matters relating to safeguards for linguistic minorities and report to the President.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: Which Article directs States and local authorities to endeavour to provide mother-tongue instruction at the primary stage for linguistic minority children?

options.A: Article 350A

questions.explanation: Article 350A directs every State and local authority to endeavour to provide adequate facilities for instruction in the mother tongue at the primary stage of education to children belonging to linguistic minority groups.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What is the difference between religious minority status and OBC status?

options.A: Minority status is based on recognition as a notified religious community or on linguistic-minority protections, while OBC status is based on social and educational backwardness under the relevant Central or State list; the categories are not interchangeable

questions.explanation: Minority status is based on recognition as a notified religious community or on linguistic-minority protections. OBC status is based on social and educational backwardness under the relevant Central or State list. The categories are not interchangeable.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: Does the Constitution provide a blanket reservation quota in public employment for every religious minority as such?

options.A: Yes, 27 per cent for all minorities
options.B: No, there is no single blanket constitutional public-employment quota for all religious minorities merely on the ground of religion; benefits must rest on valid constitutional and statutory criteria such as backward-class status or targeted welfare measures

questions.explanation: No. There is no single blanket constitutional public-employment quota for all religious minorities merely on the ground of religion. Benefits must rest on valid constitutional and statutory criteria, such as backward-class status or targeted welfare measures.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What is Pradhan Mantri Jan Vikas Karyakram?

options.A: An area-development programme intended to improve socio-economic infrastructure and basic amenities in identified minority-concentration areas, including education, health and skill development facilities
options.B: A scholarship scheme for minority students

questions.explanation: Pradhan Mantri Jan Vikas Karyakram (PMJVK) is an area-development programme intended to improve socio-economic infrastructure and basic amenities in identified minority-concentration areas, including facilities in education, health and skill development.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What is PM VIKAS?

options.A: Pradhan Mantri Virasat Ka Samvardhan, a Ministry of Minority Affairs programme supporting skill development, employability, livelihood opportunities, women's leadership and preservation of minority cultural heritage

questions.explanation: Pradhan Mantri Virasat Ka Samvardhan (PM VIKAS) is a Ministry of Minority Affairs programme supporting skill development, employability, livelihood opportunities, women's leadership and preservation of minority cultural heritage, subject to scheme guidelines.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: Why are minority safeguards important in a democracy?

options.A: They protect cultural identity, religious and linguistic freedom, equal citizenship and access to educational institutions, while helping prevent discrimination and social exclusion
options.B: They increase the population of minorities

questions.explanation: They protect cultural identity, religious and linguistic freedom, equal citizenship and access to educational institutions, while helping prevent discrimination and social exclusion.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What is gender equality?

options.A: The principle that people of all genders enjoy equal rights, dignity, opportunities, responsibilities and access to resources, without discrimination based on gender
options.D: A law prohibiting women from working

questions.explanation: Gender equality means that people of all genders enjoy equal rights, dignity, opportunities, responsibilities and access to resources, without discrimination based on gender.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What is women's empowerment?

options.A: The process of increasing women's agency, choices, capabilities, resources, safety, economic independence and participation in family, community, political and public decision-making
options.B: A scheme to provide free rations
options.C: A law to reserve all posts for women
options.D: A programme to keep women at home

questions.explanation: Women's empowerment is the process of increasing women's agency, choices, capabilities, resources, safety, economic independence and participation in family, community, political and public decision-making.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: Which Article guarantees equality before the law to women and men?

options.A: Article 14

questions.explanation: Article 14 guarantees equality before the law and equal protection of the laws to every person within the territory of India.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: Which Article prohibits discrimination on the ground of sex?

options.A: Article 15(1)

questions.explanation: Article 15(1) prohibits the State from discriminating against citizens on grounds only of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: Which Article permits special provisions for women and children?

options.A: Article 15(3)

questions.explanation: Article 15(3) permits the State to make special provisions for women and children.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: Which Article provides equality of opportunity in public employment?

options.A: Article 16

questions.explanation: Article 16 provides equality of opportunity in matters of public employment and prohibits specified forms of discrimination.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: Which Article directs equal pay for equal work for men and women?

options.A: Article 39(d)

questions.explanation: Article 39(d) directs the State to ensure equal pay for equal work for both men and women.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: Which Article provides for maternity relief and humane conditions of work?

options.A: Article 42

questions.explanation: Article 42 directs the State to make provision for just and humane conditions of work and maternity relief.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: Which Fundamental Duty requires citizens to renounce practices derogatory to the dignity of women?

options.A: Article 51A(e)

questions.explanation: Article 51A(e) makes it a Fundamental Duty to renounce practices derogatory to the dignity of women.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: Which Articles provide for reservation for women in Panchayats and Municipalities respectively?

options.A: Article 243D for Panchayats and Article 243T for Municipalities
options.B: Article 243T for Panchayats and Article 243D for Municipalities
options.C: Article 330 for Panchayats and Article 332 for Municipalities

questions.explanation: Article 243D provides reservation for women in Panchayats, and Article 243T provides reservation for women in Municipalities. Each provides for not less than one-third of the seats to be filled by direct election to be reserved for women, including seats reserved for women belonging to SCs and STs.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: Which Constitutional Amendment introduced the one-third reservation for women in Panchayats and Municipalities?

options.A: The 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendment Acts, 1992

questions.explanation: The 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendment Acts, 1992, introduced constitutional provisions for reservation of not less than one-third of directly elected seats for women in Panchayats and Municipalities respectively.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What is the Constitution (106th Amendment) Act, 2023?

options.A: It provides for reservation of approximately one-third of seats for women in the Lok Sabha, State Legislative Assemblies and the Delhi Legislative Assembly, including a share within SC/ST-reserved seats
options.C: It gives constitutional status to the NCBC
options.D: It clarifies State power to identify SEBCs

questions.explanation: The Constitution (106th Amendment) Act, 2023, provides for reservation of approximately one-third of seats for women in the Lok Sabha, State Legislative Assemblies and the Legislative Assembly of the National Capital Territory of Delhi, including a share within SC/ST-reserved seats.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: When does the women's reservation under the 106th Constitutional Amendment take effect?

options.A: Immediately on enactment in 2023
options.B: After a delimitation exercise undertaken for this purpose after publication of the relevant figures of the first census taken after commencement of the 106th Amendment Act, 2023 (Article 334A)
options.D: Only after a new Constitution is adopted

questions.explanation: Article 334A provides that the reservation takes effect after a delimitation exercise undertaken for this purpose after publication of the relevant figures of the first census taken after commencement of the 106th Amendment Act, 2023. It is therefore not an immediate reservation taking effect solely on the date of enactment.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What is the POSH Act, 2013?

options.A: The Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013, providing a framework to prevent and redress sexual harassment of women at workplaces
options.C: An Act to protect children from sexual offences

questions.explanation: The Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013, commonly called the POSH Act, provides a framework to prevent and redress sexual harassment of women at workplaces.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What is an Internal Committee under the POSH Act?

options.A: The workplace-level committee required under the POSH Act at an organisation or workplace with ten or more employees, to receive and inquire into complaints
options.B: A committee of the Supreme Court
options.D: A committee under the Dowry Prohibition Act

questions.explanation: An Internal Committee is the workplace-level committee required under the POSH Act at an organisation or workplace with ten or more employees, to receive and inquire into complaints in accordance with the Act.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What is the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005?

options.A: An Act providing civil protection and remedies for women facing domestic violence, including protection, residence, monetary relief, custody and compensation orders
options.B: A criminal law only for dowry

questions.explanation: The Act provides civil protection and remedies for women facing domestic violence, including protection, residence, monetary relief, custody and compensation orders as provided by law.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: Which Act prohibits dowry?

options.A: The Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961

questions.explanation: The Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961, prohibits the giving, taking and demanding of dowry, subject to the Act's definitions and exceptions.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: Which Act regulates maternity benefits for eligible women employees?

options.A: The Maternity Benefit Act, 1961, as amended

questions.explanation: The Maternity Benefit Act, 1961, as amended, regulates maternity benefits and related protections for eligible women employees in establishments covered by the Act.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What is the PCPNDT Act, 1994?

options.A: The Pre-Conception and Pre-Natal Diagnostic Techniques (Prohibition of Sex Selection) Act, 1994, which regulates such techniques and prohibits their misuse for sex selection

questions.explanation: The Pre-Conception and Pre-Natal Diagnostic Techniques (Prohibition of Sex Selection) Act, 1994, regulates the use of pre-conception and pre-natal diagnostic techniques and prohibits their misuse for sex selection.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What is Mission Shakti?

options.A: The Ministry of Women and Child Development's umbrella mission for women's safety, security and empowerment, with components Sambal and Samarthya and schemes such as One Stop Centres, Women Helpline, Beti Bachao Beti Padhao, PM Matru Vandana Yojana, Shakti Sadan and Sakhi Nivas

questions.explanation: Mission Shakti is the Ministry of Women and Child Development's umbrella mission for women's safety, security and empowerment. Its two broad components are Sambal and Samarthya, with services and schemes such as One Stop Centres, Women Helpline, Beti Bachao Beti Padhao, PM Matru Vandana Yojana, Shakti Sadan and Sakhi Nivas.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What is Beti Bachao Beti Padhao?

options.A: A Government of India initiative launched in 2015 to address declining child sex ratio and promote the survival, protection and education of the girl child; it is primarily an awareness and convergence programme, not a universal direct cash-transfer scheme
options.C: A scholarship for minority girls only

questions.explanation: Beti Bachao Beti Padhao is a Government of India initiative launched in 2015 to address declining child sex ratio and promote the survival, protection and education of the girl child. It is primarily an awareness and convergence programme, not a universal direct cash-transfer scheme.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What is the Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana?

options.A: A maternity benefit scheme that provides conditional financial assistance to eligible pregnant women and lactating mothers in accordance with scheme guidelines
options.D: A health insurance scheme for all

questions.explanation: Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana is a maternity benefit scheme that provides conditional financial assistance to eligible pregnant women and lactating mothers in accordance with scheme guidelines.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What are major barriers to women's equality?

options.A: Gender stereotyping, violence, unequal unpaid care work, unequal access to education and assets, discrimination in employment, wage gaps, child marriage, unsafe public spaces and under-representation in decision-making

questions.explanation: Barriers include gender stereotyping, violence, unequal unpaid care work, unequal access to education and assets, discrimination in employment, wage gaps, child marriage, unsafe public spaces and under-representation in decision-making.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: Who is generally considered a child under Indian child-protection laws?

options.A: A person below eighteen years of age under several central child-protection laws including the Juvenile Justice Act and POCSO Act; the applicable definition should always be checked as specific laws may use different age thresholds
options.B: A person below fourteen years only
options.C: A person below twenty-one years only
options.D: A person below sixteen years only

questions.explanation: Several central child-protection laws, including the Juvenile Justice Act and POCSO Act, define a child as a person below eighteen years of age. The applicable definition should always be checked because specific laws may use different age thresholds for particular purposes.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What are the main rights of children?

options.A: Survival, health, nutrition, education, protection from exploitation and violence, identity, family care, development, participation and dignity

questions.explanation: The main rights include survival, health, nutrition, education, protection from exploitation and violence, identity, family care, development, participation and dignity.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: Which Article guarantees free and compulsory education to children aged 6 to 14 years?

options.A: Article 21A

questions.explanation: Article 21A guarantees free and compulsory education to all children of the age of six to fourteen years in the manner determined by law.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: Which Act gives effect to Article 21A?

options.A: The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009, which came into force on 1 April 2010

questions.explanation: The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009, commonly called the RTE Act, came into force on 1 April 2010.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: Which Article prohibits employment of children below fourteen years in factories, mines and hazardous employment?

options.A: Article 24

questions.explanation: Article 24 prohibits employment of children below fourteen years in factories, mines or other hazardous employment.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: Which Directive Principle protects children from abuse and material abandonment?

options.A: Article 39(e)

questions.explanation: Article 39(e) directs the State to ensure that the health and strength of workers and the tender age of children are not abused and that citizens are not forced by economic necessity into unsuitable work.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: Which Directive Principle concerns opportunities for children to develop in a healthy and dignified manner?

options.A: Article 39(f)

questions.explanation: Article 39(f) directs the State to ensure that children are given opportunities and facilities to develop in a healthy manner and in conditions of freedom and dignity, and that childhood and youth are protected against exploitation and moral and material abandonment.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What does Article 45 provide?

options.A: It directs the State to endeavour to provide early childhood care and education for all children until they complete the age of six years
options.B: It guarantees free education up to age 14

questions.explanation: Article 45 directs the State to endeavour to provide early childhood care and education for all children until they complete the age of six years.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What does Article 51A(k) require of parents or guardians?

options.A: To provide opportunities for education to their child or ward between six and fourteen years of age
options.B: To send children to private schools only
options.D: To renounce practices derogatory to women

questions.explanation: Article 51A(k) makes it a Fundamental Duty of every parent or guardian to provide opportunities for education to their child or ward between six and fourteen years of age.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What is the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012?

options.A: An Act that protects children from sexual assault, sexual harassment and pornography, provides child-friendly procedures and special courts, and applies to children of all genders
options.B: An Act that provides free education
options.C: An Act that prohibits child marriage
options.D: An Act that regulates child labour

questions.explanation: The POCSO Act protects children from sexual assault, sexual harassment and pornography, provides child-friendly procedures and special courts, and applies to children of all genders.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What is the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015?

options.A: An Act that provides a framework for care, protection, development, treatment and social reintegration of children in need of care and protection and children in conflict with law

questions.explanation: The Juvenile Justice Act provides a framework for care, protection, development, treatment and social reintegration of children in need of care and protection and children in conflict with law.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What does the Child and Adolescent Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 1986, as amended, provide?

options.A: It generally prohibits employment of children below fourteen years, subject to limited statutory exceptions, and prohibits employment of adolescents aged fourteen to below eighteen years in hazardous occupations and processes specified by law
options.C: It prohibits employment of all persons below eighteen years without exception

questions.explanation: The Act generally prohibits employment of children below fourteen years, subject to limited statutory exceptions, and prohibits employment of adolescents aged fourteen to below eighteen years in hazardous occupations and processes specified by law.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What is the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006?

options.A: An Act that prohibits child marriage and provides for prevention, protection, maintenance and penalties; a male is a child if he has not completed twenty-one years and a female if she has not completed eighteen years
options.C: An Act that provides free education

questions.explanation: The Act prohibits child marriage and provides for prevention, protection, maintenance and penalties. For purposes of the Act, a male is a child if he has not completed twenty-one years and a female is a child if she has not completed eighteen years.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: Which body is the national statutory commission for protection of child rights?

options.A: The National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR), established under the Commissions for Protection of Child Rights Act, 2005

questions.explanation: The National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR) is a statutory body established under the Commissions for Protection of Child Rights Act, 2005.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What are the functions of the NCPCR?

options.A: It examines safeguards for child rights, investigates violations, reviews laws and policies, inquires into complaints, recommends remedial measures and promotes awareness and research on child rights

questions.explanation: The NCPCR examines safeguards for child rights, investigates violations, reviews laws and policies, inquires into complaints, recommends remedial measures and promotes awareness and research on child rights.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What is Mission Vatsalya?

options.A: The Ministry of Women and Child Development's umbrella framework for child protection, care and welfare, particularly for children in difficult circumstances and children in need of care and protection

questions.explanation: Mission Vatsalya is the Ministry of Women and Child Development's umbrella framework for child protection, care and welfare, particularly for children in difficult circumstances and children in need of care and protection.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What is Saksham Anganwadi and POSHAN 2.0?

options.A: An umbrella mission supporting nutrition, health and early childhood care and education for children, pregnant women, lactating mothers and specified adolescent girls through Anganwadi and related services
options.B: A scholarship scheme for SC students

questions.explanation: Saksham Anganwadi and POSHAN 2.0 is an umbrella mission supporting nutrition, health and early childhood care and education for children, pregnant women, lactating mothers and specified adolescent girls through Anganwadi and related services.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What is the Child Helpline number?
questions.explanation: The Child Helpline number is 1098. It is integrated with the emergency response framework under the current child-protection arrangements; emergency services can also be contacted through 112.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: Why is child participation important?

options.A: It means listening to children's views in matters affecting them in age- and maturity-appropriate ways, while protecting their best interests, safety and dignity
options.B: It means giving children the right to vote
options.C: It means allowing children to work
options.D: It means exempting children from education

questions.explanation: Child participation means listening to children's views in matters affecting them in age- and maturity-appropriate ways, while protecting their best interests, safety and dignity.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What is the rights-based understanding of disability under Indian law?

options.A: Under the RPwD Act, 2016, disability is understood in relation to long-term physical, mental, intellectual or sensory impairments which, in interaction with barriers, hinder full and effective participation in society equally with others
options.B: Disability is purely a medical condition with no social dimension
options.C: Disability is defined only by income

questions.explanation: Under the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016, disability is understood in relation to long-term physical, mental, intellectual or sensory impairments which, in interaction with barriers, hinder full and effective participation in society equally with others.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What is a person with benchmark disability under the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016?

options.A: A person with not less than forty per cent of a specified disability, as certified by the competent authority, subject to the Act's definition
options.B: A person with any disability however minor
options.C: A person with not less than seventy-five per cent disability
options.D: A person with a disability certificate from any doctor

questions.explanation: A person with benchmark disability is a person with not less than forty per cent of a specified disability, as certified by the competent authority, subject to the Act's definition.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: Which Act is the main central law protecting the rights of persons with disabilities in India?

options.A: The Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016

questions.explanation: The Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016, is the principal central legislation that recognises rights and entitlements of persons with disabilities and gives effect to India's obligations under the UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: How many specified disabilities are listed in the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016?

options.A: Twenty-one

questions.explanation: The Act recognises twenty-one specified disabilities in its Schedule, including physical, intellectual, developmental, sensory, neurological and blood-related conditions, and multiple disabilities.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: Which of the following disabilities is recognised under the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016?

options.A: Blindness, low vision, leprosy-cured persons, hearing impairment, locomotor disability, dwarfism, intellectual disability, mental illness, autism spectrum disorder, cerebral palsy, muscular dystrophy, chronic neurological conditions, specific learning disabilities, multiple sclerosis, speech and language disability, thalassemia, haemophilia, sickle cell disease, multiple disabilities including deafblindness, acid-attack victims and Parkinson's disease

questions.explanation: The Schedule includes blindness, low vision, leprosy-cured persons, hearing impairment, locomotor disability, dwarfism, intellectual disability, mental illness, autism spectrum disorder, cerebral palsy, muscular dystrophy, chronic neurological conditions, specific learning disabilities, multiple sclerosis, speech and language disability, thalassemia, haemophilia, sickle cell disease, multiple disabilities including deafblindness, acid-attack victims and Parkinson's disease.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: Which section of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act guarantees equality and non-discrimination?

options.A: Section 3

questions.explanation: Section 3 of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016, deals with equality and non-discrimination.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What is reasonable accommodation in disability rights?

options.A: Necessary and appropriate modifications or adjustments, without imposing a disproportionate or undue burden, to ensure that persons with disabilities can enjoy or exercise rights equally with others
options.B: A pension for persons with disabilities

questions.explanation: Reasonable accommodation means necessary and appropriate modifications or adjustments, without imposing a disproportionate or undue burden, to ensure that persons with disabilities can enjoy or exercise rights equally with others.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What is inclusive education for children with disabilities?

options.A: Educating children with and without disabilities together, with appropriate support, accessible infrastructure, learning materials, teaching methods and reasonable accommodation
options.B: Educating children with disabilities only in special schools
options.C: Educating children with disabilities at home
options.D: Excluding children with disabilities from school

questions.explanation: Inclusive education means educating children with and without disabilities together, with appropriate support, accessible infrastructure, learning materials, teaching methods and reasonable accommodation.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: Which section provides free education for children with benchmark disabilities aged 6 to 18 years?

options.A: Section 31

questions.explanation: Section 31 of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016, provides for free education for children with benchmark disabilities between six and eighteen years in an appropriate neighbourhood or special school of their choice, as provided by the Act.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What reservation is provided for persons with benchmark disabilities in government employment under the RPwD Act?

options.A: Section 34 provides for not less than four per cent of vacancies in the cadre strength in each group of posts in every Government establishment
options.B: Section 32 provides five per cent of seats
options.C: Section 34 provides ten per cent of vacancies
options.D: Section 31 provides three per cent of vacancies

questions.explanation: Section 34 provides for not less than four per cent of vacancies in the cadre strength in each group of posts in every Government establishment for persons with benchmark disabilities, subject to the Act and identification of posts.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What reservation is provided for persons with benchmark disabilities in higher educational institutions under the RPwD Act?

options.A: Section 32 requires Government higher educational institutions and other higher educational institutions receiving Government aid to reserve not less than five per cent of seats
options.B: Section 34 provides four per cent of seats
options.C: Section 31 provides ten per cent of seats
options.D: Section 40 provides three per cent of seats

questions.explanation: Section 32 requires Government higher educational institutions and other higher educational institutions receiving Government aid to reserve not less than five per cent of seats for persons with benchmark disabilities.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: Which section of the RPwD Act deals with accessibility?

options.A: Section 40

questions.explanation: Section 40 requires the Central Government to formulate accessibility standards for the physical environment, transport, information and communications, including information and communication technology and public facilities.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What is the difference between a person with disability and a person with benchmark disability?

options.A: A person with disability is defined by long-term impairment interacting with barriers to participation, while a person with benchmark disability meets the statutory threshold of at least forty per cent of a specified disability, certified as required by law, for specified entitlements such as reservation
options.C: A person with benchmark disability has any disability however minor
options.D: A person with disability must have at least forty per cent disability

questions.explanation: A person with disability is defined by long-term impairment interacting with barriers to participation. A person with benchmark disability meets the statutory threshold of at least forty per cent of a specified disability, certified as required by law, for specified entitlements such as reservation.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What is the Unique Disability ID project?

options.A: A project that aims to create a national database and issue a disability identity card to persons with disabilities, facilitating identification and access to disability-related services and benefits

questions.explanation: The Unique Disability ID (UDID) project aims to create a national database and issue a disability identity card to persons with disabilities, facilitating identification and access to disability-related services and benefits.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What is the ADIP Scheme?

options.A: The Assistance to Disabled Persons for Purchase/Fitting of Aids and Appliances Scheme, which supports eligible persons with disabilities by providing assistive devices and appliances to improve mobility, communication and daily functioning
options.B: A scholarship scheme for disabled students
options.C: A pension scheme for disabled persons

questions.explanation: The Assistance to Disabled Persons for Purchase/Fitting of Aids and Appliances (ADIP) Scheme supports eligible persons with disabilities by providing assistive devices and appliances to improve mobility, communication and daily functioning.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What is the SIPDA scheme?

options.A: The Scheme for Implementation of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, which supports implementation of disability rights provisions, including accessibility, awareness, capacity building and related initiatives

questions.explanation: The Scheme for Implementation of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act (SIPDA) supports implementation of disability rights provisions, including accessibility, awareness, capacity building and related initiatives, subject to current guidelines.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What is the social model of disability?

options.A: It explains disability as arising not only from an individual's impairment but also from environmental, institutional, communication and attitudinal barriers that restrict participation
options.B: It explains disability purely as a medical condition
options.C: It explains disability as a punishment for past deeds
options.D: It explains disability as a purely economic issue

questions.explanation: The social model explains disability as arising not only from an individual's impairment but also from environmental, institutional, communication and attitudinal barriers that restrict participation.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What is accessibility?

options.A: Designing buildings, transport, services, information, communication and digital systems so that persons with disabilities can use them safely and independently, to the greatest extent possible
options.C: Providing pensions to persons with disabilities
options.D: Reserving all government jobs for persons with disabilities

questions.explanation: Accessibility means designing buildings, transport, services, information, communication and digital systems so that persons with disabilities can use them safely and independently, to the greatest extent possible.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: Which international convention is important for disability rights, and when did India ratify it?

options.A: The United Nations Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (UNCRPD), adopted in 2006; India ratified it in 2007
options.B: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights, adopted in 1948
options.C: The International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights, adopted in 1966
options.D: The Convention on the Rights of the Child, adopted in 1989

questions.explanation: The United Nations Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (UNCRPD), adopted in 2006, is the major international human-rights convention on disability rights. India ratified it in 2007.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What is social welfare?

options.A: Organised policies, services and programmes designed to improve people's well-being, protect vulnerable groups, reduce deprivation and provide support in areas such as health, education, housing, nutrition, livelihood and social security
options.D: A scheme for government employees only

questions.explanation: Social welfare refers to organised policies, services and programmes designed to improve people's well-being, protect vulnerable groups, reduce deprivation and provide support in areas such as health, education, housing, nutrition, livelihood and social security.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What is social security?

options.A: Protection provided by the State or other institutions against major life risks and economic insecurity, such as old age, disability, sickness, unemployment, maternity, loss of a breadwinner and poverty

questions.explanation: Social security is protection provided by the State or other institutions against major life risks and economic insecurity, such as old age, disability, sickness, unemployment, maternity, loss of a breadwinner and poverty.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What is the difference between social welfare and social security?

options.A: Social welfare is a broad concept covering services and programmes that improve well-being, while social security is a more specific set of protections against defined social and economic risks
options.C: Social security is broader than social welfare
options.D: Social welfare applies only to government employees

questions.explanation: Social welfare is a broad concept covering services and programmes that improve well-being. Social security is a more specific set of protections against defined social and economic risks.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What is a welfare state in the context of social welfare?

options.A: A State that accepts responsibility for ensuring minimum standards of living, access to essential services and protection against vulnerability through public policy, social insurance, assistance and regulation
options.B: A State that provides only defence
options.C: A State that does not intervene in welfare
options.D: A State that taxes only the rich

questions.explanation: A welfare state accepts responsibility for ensuring minimum standards of living, access to essential services and protection against vulnerability through public policy, social insurance, assistance and regulation.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: Which Parts of the Constitution are especially important for social welfare?

options.A: Part II contains enforceable Fundamental Rights, while Part IV contains Directive Principles of State Policy that guide the State in promoting welfare, social and economic justice, public health, education, work and protection of weaker sections

questions.explanation: Part II contains enforceable Fundamental Rights, while Part IV contains Directive Principles of State Policy that guide the State in promoting welfare, social and economic justice, public health, education, work and protection of weaker sections.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: Which Article directs the State to raise nutrition, standard of living and public health?

options.A: Article 47

questions.explanation: Article 47 makes improvement of nutrition, standard of living and public health among the primary duties of the State.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What is the National Social Assistance Programme?

options.A: A social assistance programme that includes pensions for eligible older persons, widows and persons with disabilities, and family benefit support for eligible households, under applicable guidelines
options.B: A scholarship scheme for SC students

questions.explanation: The National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP) is a social assistance programme that includes pensions for eligible older persons, widows and persons with disabilities, and family benefit support for eligible households, under applicable guidelines.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What is Direct Benefit Transfer?

options.A: A mechanism through which eligible benefits are transferred directly to beneficiaries' bank accounts, with the aim of improving transparency, reducing intermediaries and supporting timely delivery
options.B: A scheme to transfer posts between departments
options.C: A method of giving cash to intermediaries

questions.explanation: Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) is a mechanism through which eligible benefits are transferred directly to beneficiaries' bank accounts, with the aim of improving transparency, reducing intermediaries and supporting timely delivery.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What is a social audit?

options.A: A process through which people examine public records, expenditure, implementation and outcomes of a public programme, and verify whether benefits reached intended beneficiaries
options.B: An audit conducted by a private chartered accountant only
options.C: A government inspection without public participation

questions.explanation: A social audit is a process through which people examine public records, expenditure, implementation and outcomes of a public programme, and verify whether benefits reached intended beneficiaries.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What is the role of self-help groups in social welfare?

options.A: They promote savings, credit access, mutual support, livelihoods, collective decision-making and community participation, and often strengthen the economic and social position of women

questions.explanation: Self-help groups promote savings, credit access, mutual support, livelihoods, collective decision-making and community participation, and often strengthen the economic and social position of women.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What is the role of local self-government in social welfare?

options.A: Panchayats and Municipalities help identify local needs, plan and implement development activities, deliver or monitor public services and enable people's participation, according to constitutional provisions and State laws

questions.explanation: Panchayats and Municipalities help identify local needs, plan and implement development activities, deliver or monitor public services and enable people's participation, according to constitutional provisions and State laws.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: Name major Central Government institutions dealing with social welfare and vulnerable groups.

options.A: The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Ministry of Tribal Affairs, Ministry of Minority Affairs, Ministry of Women and Child Development, Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities, and relevant commissions and statutory bodies
options.C: Only the Ministry of Home Affairs

questions.explanation: Important institutions include the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Ministry of Tribal Affairs, Ministry of Minority Affairs, Ministry of Women and Child Development, Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities, and relevant commissions and statutory bodies.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What is PM-AJAY as a social welfare measure?

options.A: It supports socio-economic development of Scheduled Caste communities through livelihood generation, infrastructure in SC-dominated villages and educational and residential support
options.D: It is a disability pension scheme

questions.explanation: PM-AJAY supports socio-economic development of Scheduled Caste communities through livelihood generation, infrastructure in SC-dominated villages and educational and residential support.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What is the purpose of Eklavya Model Residential Schools in social welfare?

options.A: They provide residential schooling for Scheduled Tribe students, particularly in remote areas, to improve access to quality education
options.B: They provide residential schooling for minority students
options.C: They provide pensions to tribal elders
options.D: They provide skill training to SC students

questions.explanation: EMRS provide residential schooling for Scheduled Tribe students, particularly in remote areas, to improve access to quality education.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What is the purpose of PMJVK in social welfare?

options.A: It addresses infrastructure deficits in identified minority-concentration areas by supporting facilities such as schools, health centres, skill centres, hostels and community infrastructure
options.B: It provides scholarships to SC students
options.D: It provides assistive devices to persons with disabilities

questions.explanation: PMJVK addresses infrastructure deficits in identified minority-concentration areas by supporting facilities such as schools, health centres, skill centres, hostels and community infrastructure.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: Why is coordination between departments important in social welfare?

options.A: Many social problems overlap; coordinated planning helps avoid duplication, close service gaps, connect beneficiaries to multiple services and improve the overall effectiveness of welfare programmes
options.B: It reduces the need for any schemes
options.C: It eliminates the need for local self-government

questions.explanation: Many social problems overlap. Coordinated planning helps avoid duplication, close service gaps, connect beneficiaries to multiple services and improve the overall effectiveness of welfare programmes.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What is reservation in India?

options.A: A constitutionally enabled measure that sets aside a specified share of seats, posts or opportunities for eligible categories in areas such as public employment, education and elected representation

questions.explanation: Reservation is a constitutionally enabled measure that sets aside a specified share of seats, posts or opportunities for eligible categories in areas such as public employment, education and elected representation, subject to relevant constitutional provisions and laws.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What is the constitutional objective of reservation?

options.A: To address historical and structural disadvantage, improve representation, expand access to education and public employment, and make equality more substantive
options.C: To increase the income of the rich

questions.explanation: Reservation aims to address historical and structural disadvantage, improve representation, expand access to education and public employment, and make equality more substantive.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: Which Article provides equality before the law?

options.A: Article 14

questions.explanation: Article 14 guarantees equality before the law and equal protection of the laws to every person.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: Which Article prohibits discrimination and permits specified special provisions for disadvantaged classes?

options.A: Article 15

questions.explanation: Article 15 prohibits specified forms of discrimination and contains enabling clauses, including clauses (4), (5) and (6), for special provisions for backward classes, Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and Economically Weaker Sections under stated conditions.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: Which Article is the main enabling provision for reservation in public employment for inadequately represented backward classes?

options.A: Article 16(4)

questions.explanation: Article 16(4) enables reservation of appointments or posts in favour of a backward class of citizens that is not adequately represented in State services, in the opinion of the State.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: Which Article enables reservation in promotion for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes?

options.A: Article 16(4A)

questions.explanation: Article 16(4A) enables reservation in promotion, with consequential seniority, for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes that are inadequately represented in State services, subject to constitutional requirements.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: Which Article provides for EWS reservation in educational institutions?

options.A: Article 15(6), inserted by the 103rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 2019

questions.explanation: Article 15(6), inserted by the 103rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 2019, enables special provisions, including reservation of up to ten per cent, for Economically Weaker Sections in educational institutions, subject to constitutional conditions and exclusions.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: Which Article provides for EWS reservation in public employment?

options.A: Article 16(6), inserted by the 103rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 2019

questions.explanation: Article 16(6), inserted by the 103rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 2019, enables reservation of up to ten per cent of appointments or posts for Economically Weaker Sections in addition to existing reservation, subject to constitutional conditions.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: Which Constitutional Amendment introduced EWS reservation?

options.A: The 103rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 2019

questions.explanation: The Constitution (103rd Amendment) Act, 2019, inserted Articles 15(6) and 16(6) to enable special provisions, including up to ten per cent reservation, for Economically Weaker Sections.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: Who can generally qualify for EWS reservation under the Central Government framework?

options.A: Persons not covered by the existing reservation schemes for SCs, STs and socially and educationally backward classes, who satisfy the prescribed family-income and asset criteria; under the Central criteria reported in 2026, annual family income below Rs. 8 lakh is one condition, along with specified asset-based exclusions
options.B: All persons below the poverty line

questions.explanation: EWS reservation is meant for persons who are not covered by the existing reservation schemes for SCs, STs and socially and educationally backward classes, and who satisfy the prescribed family-income and asset criteria. Under the Central Government criteria reported in 2026, annual family income below Rs. 8 lakh is one condition, along with specified asset-based exclusions.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What asset-based exclusions are relevant to Central EWS eligibility?

options.A: A family is excluded irrespective of income if it owns or possesses five acres or more of agricultural land, a residential flat of 1,000 square feet or more, a residential plot of 100 square yards or more in a notified municipality, or a residential plot of 200 square yards or more elsewhere
options.C: Only ownership of agricultural land above ten acres
options.D: Only ownership of a house in a village

questions.explanation: Under the Central criteria reported in 2026, a family is excluded irrespective of income if it owns or possesses five acres or more of agricultural land, a residential flat of 1,000 square feet or more, a residential plot of 100 square yards or more in a notified municipality, or a residential plot of 200 square yards or more elsewhere. Candidates must follow the current prescribed certificate rules.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What is vertical reservation?

options.A: Reservation for distinct social categories such as Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, Other Backward Classes and Economically Weaker Sections, with each category having a specified share under the relevant rules
options.B: Reservation that cuts across vertical categories
options.D: Reservation only for persons with disabilities

questions.explanation: Vertical reservation is reservation for distinct social categories such as Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, Other Backward Classes and Economically Weaker Sections, with each category having a specified share under the relevant rules.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What is horizontal reservation?

options.A: Reservation that cuts across vertical categories and applies to groups such as persons with benchmark disabilities, women or ex-servicemen, adjusted within the relevant vertical categories according to the governing rules
options.B: Reservation for SCs, STs, OBCs and EWS separately

questions.explanation: Horizontal reservation cuts across vertical categories and applies to groups such as persons with benchmark disabilities and, under particular laws or policies, women or ex-servicemen. It is adjusted within the relevant vertical categories according to the governing rules.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What is the difference between vertical and horizontal reservation?

options.A: Vertical reservation provides separate shares for specified social categories, while horizontal reservation operates across those categories and is adjusted within them, rather than necessarily being added as a separate vertical block
options.C: Horizontal reservation is for SCs only
options.D: Vertical reservation is for women only

questions.explanation: Vertical reservation provides separate shares for specified social categories. Horizontal reservation operates across those categories and is adjusted within them, rather than necessarily being added as a separate vertical block.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What are the Central Government reservation percentages for SCs, STs and OBCs in direct recruitment on an all-India basis by open competition?

options.A: 15 per cent for SCs, 7.5 per cent for STs and 27 per cent for OBCs
options.B: 10 per cent for SCs, 5 per cent for STs and 20 per cent for OBCs
options.C: 20 per cent for SCs, 10 per cent for STs and 30 per cent for OBCs
options.D: 15 per cent for SCs, 7.5 per cent for STs and 10 per cent for OBCs

questions.explanation: The standard Central Government percentages are 15 per cent for Scheduled Castes, 7.5 per cent for Scheduled Tribes and 27 per cent for Other Backward Classes, in direct recruitment on an all-India basis by open competition.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What is the EWS reservation percentage enabled for Central Government civil posts and services?

options.A: Up to ten per cent for eligible Economically Weaker Sections, subject to applicable rules and recruitment instructions

questions.explanation: The constitutional framework enables reservation of up to ten per cent for eligible Economically Weaker Sections in civil posts and services, subject to applicable rules and recruitment instructions.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What is the total of the standard SC, ST and OBC percentages in Central Government all-India direct recruitment by open competition?

options.A: 49.5 per cent

questions.explanation: The standard percentages of 15 per cent for SCs, 7.5 per cent for STs and 27 per cent for OBCs add up to 49.5 per cent.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: Does the 10 per cent EWS provision replace the SC, ST and OBC reservations?

options.A: No, EWS reservation is a separate provision under Articles 15(6) and 16(6), designed for eligible economically weaker persons who are not covered by the existing SC, ST and SEBC reservation schemes
options.D: Yes, it replaces SC and ST reservation

questions.explanation: No. EWS reservation is a separate provision under Articles 15(6) and 16(6), designed for eligible economically weaker persons who are not covered by the existing SC, ST and SEBC reservation schemes.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: Which Supreme Court case is associated with the general 50 per cent ceiling on reservation under Articles 15(4) and 16(4)?

options.A: Indra Sawhney v. Union of India (1992)
options.B: Janhit Abhiyan v. Union of India (2022)

questions.explanation: Indra Sawhney v. Union of India, decided in 1992, laid down the general rule that reservations under Articles 15(4) and 16(4) should ordinarily not exceed 50 per cent, subject to exceptional circumstances recognised by law.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: Which Supreme Court case upheld the 103rd Constitutional Amendment providing EWS reservation?

options.A: Janhit Abhiyan v. Union of India (2022), by a 3:2 majority
options.B: Indra Sawhney v. Union of India (1992)

questions.explanation: Janhit Abhiyan v. Union of India, decided in 2022, upheld the 103rd Constitutional Amendment by a 3:2 majority.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: Does the 50 per cent rule under Indra Sawhney automatically invalidate the separate EWS provision?

options.A: No, the Supreme Court upheld the 103rd Amendment in Janhit Abhiyan and treated the EWS provisions under Articles 15(6) and 16(6) as a distinct constitutional basis; the general rule for Articles 15(4) and 16(4) must be distinguished from the separate EWS clauses
options.B: Yes, EWS reservation was struck down
options.C: Yes, but only for educational institutions
options.D: No, but EWS reservation applies only to STs

questions.explanation: No. The Supreme Court upheld the 103rd Amendment in Janhit Abhiyan and treated the EWS provisions under Articles 15(6) and 16(6) as a distinct constitutional basis. Candidates should distinguish the general rule for Articles 15(4) and 16(4) from the separate EWS clauses.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What is the reservation for persons with benchmark disabilities in Government establishments under the RPwD Act, 2016?

options.A: Section 34 provides not less than four per cent reservation in vacancies in the cadre strength in each group of posts in every Government establishment
options.B: Section 32 provides five per cent of seats
options.C: Section 34 provides ten per cent of vacancies
options.D: Section 31 provides three per cent of vacancies

questions.explanation: Section 34 provides not less than four per cent reservation in vacancies in the cadre strength in each group of posts in every Government establishment for persons with benchmark disabilities, subject to the Act.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What is the reservation for persons with benchmark disabilities in eligible higher education institutions?

options.A: Section 32 of the RPwD Act, 2016, requires Government higher educational institutions and other higher educational institutions receiving Government aid to reserve not less than five per cent of seats
options.B: Section 34 provides four per cent of seats
options.C: Section 31 provides ten per cent of seats
options.D: Section 40 provides three per cent of seats

questions.explanation: Section 32 of the RPwD Act, 2016, requires Government higher educational institutions and other higher educational institutions receiving Government aid to reserve not less than five per cent of seats for persons with benchmark disabilities.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What is the reservation for women in Panchayats and Municipalities?

options.A: Articles 243D and 243T provide for reservation of not less than one-third of directly elected seats for women in Panchayats and Municipalities respectively; State laws may provide a higher share

questions.explanation: Articles 243D and 243T provide for reservation of not less than one-third of directly elected seats for women in Panchayats and Municipalities respectively; State laws may provide a higher share.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What is the one-third women's reservation in Parliament and State Assemblies?

options.A: The 106th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2023, inserted provisions for one-third reservation for women in the Lok Sabha, State Legislative Assemblies and the Delhi Legislative Assembly, with implementation linked to the census and delimitation process stated in Article 334A

questions.explanation: The 106th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2023, inserted provisions for one-third reservation for women in the Lok Sabha, State Legislative Assemblies and the Delhi Legislative Assembly, with implementation linked to the census and delimitation process stated in Article 334A.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: Does a candidate from a reserved category have to compete only for reserved vacancies?

options.A: No, eligible candidates from reserved categories may also compete for unreserved vacancies on merit; an unreserved vacancy is open to all eligible candidates and is not reserved for any caste or community
options.B: Yes, they can compete only for reserved vacancies
options.C: Yes, they are barred from unreserved vacancies
options.D: No, but only for SC candidates

questions.explanation: No. Eligible candidates from reserved categories may also compete for unreserved vacancies on merit. An unreserved vacancy is open to all eligible candidates and is not reserved for any caste or community.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What is the difference between a reserved vacancy and an unreserved vacancy?

options.A: A reserved vacancy is earmarked for eligible candidates of the specified category under applicable rules, while an unreserved vacancy is open to all eligible candidates regardless of category
options.B: A reserved vacancy is open to all; an unreserved vacancy is for SCs only
options.D: An unreserved vacancy is for OBCs only

questions.explanation: A reserved vacancy is earmarked for eligible candidates of the specified category under applicable rules. An unreserved vacancy is open to all eligible candidates regardless of category.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: Are Central Government reservation percentages automatically applicable to Karnataka State recruitment?

options.A: No, Central Government percentages and lists must not be automatically applied to State recruitment; Karnataka State recruitment is governed by the applicable State laws, Government Orders, roster rules, category lists and the specific recruitment notification
options.C: Yes, but only for SC and ST

questions.explanation: No. Central Government percentages and lists must not be automatically applied to State recruitment. Karnataka State recruitment is governed by the applicable State laws, Government Orders, roster rules, category lists and the specific recruitment notification.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: Why must candidates verify caste, income and disability certificates before applying for reservation?

options.A: Reservation benefits depend on valid certificates issued by competent authorities, the correct Central or State list, non-creamy-layer or EWS conditions where applicable, benchmark-disability certification where required, and the cut-off dates and formats specified in the recruitment notification
options.D: Only a ration card is needed

questions.explanation: Reservation benefits depend on valid certificates issued by competent authorities, the correct Central or State list, non-creamy-layer or EWS conditions where applicable, benchmark-disability certification where required, and the cut-off dates and formats specified in the recruitment notification.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What is affirmative action?

options.A: Deliberate measures adopted by the State or institutions to improve access, representation and opportunities for groups that have experienced historical or structural disadvantage

questions.explanation: Affirmative action refers to deliberate measures adopted by the State or institutions to improve access, representation and opportunities for groups that have experienced historical or structural disadvantage.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What is the main objective of affirmative action?

options.A: To reduce structural barriers, correct under-representation, improve equal opportunity and make constitutional equality effective in practice

questions.explanation: Its objective is to reduce structural barriers, correct under-representation, improve equal opportunity and make constitutional equality effective in practice.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: Is reservation the only form of affirmative action?

options.A: No, reservation is one form; other measures include scholarships, fee support, hostels, coaching, skill development, accessible infrastructure, targeted health and nutrition services, financial assistance and anti-discrimination safeguards
options.B: Yes, reservation is the only form

questions.explanation: No. Reservation is one form of affirmative action. Other measures include scholarships, fee support, hostels, coaching, skill development, accessible infrastructure, targeted health and nutrition services, financial assistance and anti-discrimination safeguards.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What is the difference between reservation and affirmative action?

options.A: Reservation is a specific measure that sets aside a share of seats or posts for eligible categories, while affirmative action is a broader set of positive measures, of which reservation is only one instrument
options.C: Affirmative action is narrower than reservation
options.D: Reservation is broader than affirmative action

questions.explanation: Reservation is a specific measure that sets aside a share of seats or posts for eligible categories. Affirmative action is a broader set of positive measures, of which reservation is only one instrument.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What is positive discrimination?

options.A: A commonly used expression for special measures that provide support or preferential treatment to disadvantaged groups in order to reduce entrenched inequalities; in Indian constitutional discussion, the term is often used alongside affirmative action or protective discrimination

questions.explanation: Positive discrimination is a commonly used expression for special measures that provide support or preferential treatment to disadvantaged groups in order to reduce entrenched inequalities. In Indian constitutional discussion, the term is often used alongside affirmative action or protective discrimination.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: What is protective discrimination in the Indian constitutional context?

options.A: Constitutionally permitted special provisions designed to protect disadvantaged groups and advance substantive equality, such as special provisions under Articles 15(4) and 15(5) and reservation under relevant clauses of Article 16

questions.explanation: Protective discrimination refers to constitutionally permitted special provisions designed to protect disadvantaged groups and advance substantive equality, such as special provisions under Articles 15(4) and 15(5) and reservation under relevant clauses of Article 16.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: How do scholarships contribute to affirmative action?

options.A: They reduce financial barriers to education, help improve retention and completion, and expand access to higher education for eligible disadvantaged students
options.D: They provide pensions to the elderly

questions.explanation: Scholarships reduce financial barriers to education, help improve retention and completion, and expand access to higher education for eligible disadvantaged students.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: How do hostels and residential schools contribute to affirmative action?

options.A: They can reduce distance, housing, safety and access barriers for students from remote, poor or marginalised communities
options.D: They provide pensions to the elderly

questions.explanation: Hostels and residential schools can reduce distance, housing, safety and access barriers for students from remote, poor or marginalised communities.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: How does accessible infrastructure support affirmative action for persons with disabilities?

options.A: Accessible buildings, transport, digital platforms, communication formats and reasonable accommodation remove barriers and enable persons with disabilities to participate equally in education, employment and public life
options.B: It provides pensions to persons with disabilities
options.C: It reserves all jobs for persons with disabilities

questions.explanation: Accessible buildings, transport, digital platforms, communication formats and reasonable accommodation remove barriers and enable persons with disabilities to participate equally in education, employment and public life.

questions.subject: Social Justice
questions.question: How do anti-discrimination laws and affirmative measures work together?
